note: THE DELIVERY-MARKER LEADING-LINE BOUNDARY. One statement, two implementations, graded from here.
`.github#2544` collapsed this rule inside the engine and its round-1 repair re-created a weaker
version of the same hazard ACROSS the F#/Python language boundary: `DeliveryApplication.leadingLine`
and `check-kit-published-coherence.py`'s `_leading_line` each held their own copy of the CommonMark
indent limit, each side pinned its copy with its own fixture legs, and the only coupling was two
prose sentences that nothing read. A one-sided edit reds that side. A COORDINATED one-sided edit --
moving one language's constant AND updating that same language's legs -- passed both. That is what a
careful engineer does when they believe they are fixing a bug, and the fixtures agreed the whole way.
`.github#2563` closes it with this file. Both sides now consume THIS corpus and neither keeps a private
leg asserting a SINGLE COMMENT BODY's declares/inert verdict, so there is nowhere for a coordinated edit
to hide: move one language's constant and it reds against these verdicts; edit these verdicts to restore
it and the OTHER language reds instead.
WHAT THIS CORPUS DOES NOT SUBSUME, stated because an earlier draft claimed it subsumed everything and
that was false. `DeliveryApplicationTests.fs` retains four `.github#2544` legs whose bodies are
four-space-indented in the DECLARATION form (:304's shared `indentedSample`, used at :307 and :492, plus
:318's declaration+receipt pair). The corpus cannot absorb them: :307 and :318 are MULTI-COMMENT
scenarios that a one-body-one-verdict table cannot express -- and :318 turns on a
`fsgg:delivery-receipt` marker `obligation_declarations` never parses, so Python has no answer even in
principle -- while :492 asserts the engine's diagnostic WORDING, which the gate does not emit. Those
legs make the F# side STRICTER, never more permissive, so they cannot mask a divergence: under a
coordinated one-sided F# edit they red alongside these entries (`Failed: 4, Passed: 801`).
THE RESIDUAL, precisely: this corpus couples SINGLE-COMMENT BODIES ONLY. Multi-comment scenarios and
diagnostic wording stay engine-side by necessity, and a shape no entry enumerates is not coupled at all.
CONSUMERS -- each drives its own side's REAL entry point, never the private helper:
* F#     tests/FS.GG.Coord.Cli.Lifecycle.Tests/DeliveryApplicationTests.fs
-> DeliveryApplication.obligationsFromComments
* Python tests/kit-published-coherence/run.sh
-> check-kit-published-coherence.py --obligation-arm -> obligation_declarations
Each consumer independently asserts a STATED literal entry count. That literal lives in the two
consumers and deliberately NOT in this file: a count stored here could be edited in the same breath
as the entry it counts, which is the vacuity `.github#2534` (empty-corpus green) and `.github#1768`
(157 passing legs while the script died mid-run) both measured. Adding or removing an entry is
therefore a three-file edit, on purpose.
WHY A CORPUS AND NOT A GENERATED CONSTANT (work/2563-cross-language-indent-limit DEC-001): the rule
has four clauses -- leading blank lines are not indentation; 0-3 spaces still lead; 4+ spaces or ANY
tab is a code block; and in that case the line is returned AS WRITTEN so no prefix can match. A
shared constant couples only the numeral, leaving the other three uncoupled, and would need a
build-order dependency the Python gate's job does not have -- kit-published-coherence.yml's fixture
job installs Python only, by design. A source-text check asserts the literal rather than the
behaviour and goes vacuous on any reformatting. Deleting the Python implementation was refused
because the obligation arm must classify comment bodies with no built engine and no network.
ONLY THE DECLARATION FORM LIVES HERE, and that is a real limit rather than an oversight. The
`<!-- fsgg:delivery-obligations none ... -->` form is skipped by `obligation_declarations` by design,
so Python answers `no declarations` for it whether it is indented or not and has no verdict to
compare. The engine's `none`-form indent legs therefore stay in the F# suite, where they remain
meaningful. There is deliberately NO per-entry skip flag: an opt-out in the artifact whose whole
purpose is to prevent an opt-out would be the first thing a coordinated edit reached for.
`head` is the head SHA both consumers pass to their entry point; the engine matches it against each
marker's `head=` field and the gate does not read it. `verdict` is `declares` (the engine returns the
obligation, and the gate names it) or `inert` (the engine returns an Error that NAMES the
leading-line rule -- criterion 5 requires inert AND named -- and the gate reports no declaration).
head: head-a

entries.name: spaces-0
entries.why: No indentation at all: the marker is the comment's leading line by inspection.

entries.name: spaces-1
entries.why: One space renders as nothing. `.github#2544`: `gh api --field` payloads and comment editors add leading whitespace for free, so an arm that stayed byte-0 would call a LIVE declaration absent.

entries.name: spaces-2
entries.why: Two spaces render as nothing.

entries.name: spaces-3
entries.why: THREE SPACES IS THE BOUNDARY FROM BELOW. This is the widest indentation CommonMark still renders as an ordinary paragraph, so the marker is the leading line in every sense a reader has access to. Moving the limit up makes this entry the one that reds.

entries.name: spaces-4
entries.why: FOUR SPACES IS THE BOUNDARY FROM ABOVE. CommonMark opens an INDENTED CODE BLOCK here, so the marker is a visible code sample. Reading it as a declaration is the `.github#2544` round-1 fail-open: a bystander's indented sample destroyed a valid declaration already on somebody else's PR.

entries.name: spaces-5
entries.why: Past the boundary.

entries.name: spaces-6
entries.why: Past the boundary.

entries.name: tab
entries.why: A tab is one tab stop. Tab stops are every 4 columns, so a leading tab always lands at column 4 or beyond and ALWAYS opens an indented code block.

entries.name: space-tab
entries.why: Tab arrangement 2 of 5. There is no arrangement of 0-3 spaces and a tab that CommonMark leaves as a paragraph, so `any tab in the indent` and `>= 4 columns` coincide exactly.

entries.name: three-spaces-tab
entries.why: Tab arrangement 3 of 5, and the tightest: three spaces then a tab still reaches a tab stop.

entries.name: tab-three-spaces
entries.why: Tab arrangement 4 of 5.

entries.name: two-tabs
entries.why: Tab arrangement 5 of 5.

entries.name: nl-spaces-0
entries.why: A leading blank line is not indentation. This is the shape heredocs produce, and the one `.github#2544` was filed about.

entries.name: nlnl-spaces-3
entries.why: Blank lines above a marker indented to the boundary from below: both tolerances at once.

entries.name: crlf-spaces-3
entries.why: CRLF case 1 of 2. Normalization must happen before the indent is measured, or `\r` counts as content.

entries.name: nl-spaces-4
entries.why: A leading blank line does not buy indentation tolerance: the first CONTENT line is still a code block.

entries.name: nl-tab
entries.why: Same, for the tab clause.

entries.name: crlf-spaces-4
entries.why: CRLF case 2 of 2.

entries.name: blank-line-of-spaces
entries.why: THE TRAP THAT LOOKS LIKE THE OPPOSITE ONE: the first line is four spaces, but it is BLANK, so it is not the first CONTENT line. The marker at byte 0 of line 2 declares. A reader who measures the first line rather than the first non-empty line gets this backwards.

entries.name: prose-first
entries.body:
Here is what I owe:

<!-- fsgg:delivery-obligation id=prose-first kind=package-release head=head-a -->
entries.why: `Leading line` means the FIRST content line, not `anywhere in the comment`. A marker below prose is a mention, not a declaration.

entries.name: fenced
entries.why: The fence is the comment's leading line, so the marker on line 2 is not a declaration. `.github#2347` acceptance 2 and the `.github#2264` round-1 anchoring fix are what this entry holds in place.
